macro: This is a company-specific earnings digest for Thursday October 15th, focused on pre-market reporters. There is no broad index or overnight macro commentary provided in this edition. Risk tone is mixed given the blend of beats, inline prints, and one major negative preannouncement.
rates_fed: No explicit Fed or rates commentary is included in this newsletter. However, PNC notes that residential and commercial mortgage income fell due to fallout from high rates, suggesting the rate environment remains a headwind for rate-sensitive businesses.
market_outlook: No explicit directional market call is made by Adam in this edition. The overall earnings tone is modestly positive for financials, with several EPS beats, but FMC's aggressive negative preannouncement is a notable drag on the industrials/materials space.
bull_case: Regional and custody banks are broadly beating on EPS with margin expansion, lower provisions, and improving fee revenue trends, suggesting the financial sector is in solid fundamental shape. BNY posted 24% EPS growth and PNC and USB both beat on efficiency and credit quality. Schwab's surging client assets and trading volumes point to healthy retail investor engagement.
bear_case: FMC's massive negative preannouncement signals serious channel inventory problems in the agricultural chemicals space, which could pressure the broader materials and ag-chem complex. PNC's expense guidance moved higher and revenue missed slightly, while NII across multiple banks came in light, hinting at lingering net interest margin pressure. Manpower's inline quarter with a slightly below-consensus Q4 guide suggests no clear inflection in the labor market yet.

company_items.summary: KMB preannounced mixed Q3 results with adjusted EPS of $1.70 beating the Street's $1.60, but organic sales fell 1.3% versus the consensus estimate of -0.7%. Full-year guidance was reiterated, offering no incremental upside. The volume softness is a modest negative offset by the earnings outperformance.

Penske Auto will be taken private by Penske Corp. and Mitsui at $212 per share in cash, valuing the deal at $16.3 billion. This represents a significant premium and removes PAG from the public market. The deal is straightforwardly bullish for existing shareholders.

BNY delivered strong Q3 results with EPS up 24% to $2.37 versus the Street's $2.27, driven by revenue growth of 12% to $5.676 billion and 180 basis points of pre-tax margin expansion year over year. Issuer services fees surged 43% and FX revenue rose 19%, highlighting the strength of its fee-based business model. Management flagged a constructive but uneven operating environment.

FHN reported an EPS loss of 20 cents in Q3 due to a deliberate balance sheet restructuring, though adjusted EPS of 53 cents was in line with consensus. The company agreed to sell approximately $4.5 billion of lower-yielding consumer mortgages, a move expected to be accretive to earnings and free up capacity for future loan growth. The headline loss masks a strategically constructive repositioning.

Marsh reported Q3 EPS of $2.03, a few cents above the Street's $1.96, with aggregate organic revenue growth of 5% beating the 4% consensus. Consulting segment delivered standout 8% organic growth versus the 4.8% estimate, though Reinsurance was weak at -6%. Overall a modestly positive print driven by the consulting outperformance.

PNC beat on Q3 adjusted EPS at $5.09 versus the $4.96 consensus, aided by better efficiency at 57% and significantly lower provisions of $189 million against the $246 million estimate, though revenue of $6.562 billion slightly missed. The 2026 guidance update is mixed — revenue growth guidance moved up to 13.7% from 13% but expense growth also increased to 9.5% from 8.5%. Mortgage income fell 6% sequentially and 16% year over year due to the high-rate environment.

Schwab posted Q3 EPS of $1.69, up 20% and a few cents above the $1.65 estimate, with revenue of $7.17 billion in line and margins expanding 350 basis points to 54.8%. Total client assets rose 15% to $13.33 trillion and core net new assets surged 38% to $190.4 billion, while margin loan balances jumped 14% sequentially to $187.9 billion and daily average trading volume rose 44% year over year. NII and NIM were slightly light but the asset and engagement metrics are clearly strong.

USB reported Q3 EPS of $1.34, essentially in line with the $1.33 consensus, as better efficiency and lower provisions offset slightly weaker revenue of $7.97 billion versus the $8.01 billion estimate. Fee revenue accelerated to 14.9% growth, though ex-BTIG the underlying trend cooled to 7.6%. Full-year revenue guidance was raised to up 6-7% ex-BTIG with operating leverage expanding to approximately 400 basis points from the prior 300-plus basis points.

FMC issued a major negative preannouncement for Q3, citing weaker-than-expected demand and elevated inventory of higher-priced FMC products at channel customers limiting replenishment. The company is aggressively slashing prices on select products and modifying its US selling and pricing model to clear the channel. This is a significant bearish catalyst for the stock and potentially for the broader agricultural chemicals sector.

Manpower reported Q3 EPS of $1.01, essentially in line with the $1.02 consensus, with organic growth of 6% slightly above the 5.75% estimate. The Q4 EPS guidance midpoint of $1.08 is just below the $1.10 Street estimate, a modest miss. Management called 2026 an inflection point for the business citing sequential improvement in Experis and Talent Solutions, but the guide doesn't fully confirm that conviction.

sectors: Financials are broadly solid this morning with multiple EPS beats across custody banking, regional banking, and brokerage — BNY, PNC, Schwab, and Marsh all topped estimates, while USB was inline and FHN's restructuring is strategically sound. Agricultural chemicals are under pressure following FMC's large negative preannouncement around channel inventory and pricing, which could reprice the ag-chem complex lower. The staffing sector remains in a murky inflection with Manpower's in-line print and slightly soft Q4 guide.
tts_summary:
Good morning. This is the earnings digest for Thursday October 15th. There is no macro or Fed commentary in today's note — this edition is entirely focused on pre-market company results, and there is a lot to work through.

Starting with the big picture across financials: the sector is broadly in good shape this morning. Bank of New York was the standout, posting earnings per share up 24 percent to two dollars and 37 cents against a two-27 estimate, with revenue up 12 percent and pre-tax margins expanding 180 basis points year over year. Issuer services fees surged 43 percent and foreign exchange revenue rose 19 percent — this is a clean, high-quality beat.

Schwab also delivered, with earnings per share up 20 percent to one-69 versus the one-65 estimate. More importantly, margins expanded 350 basis points to 54.8 percent, client assets rose 15 percent to over 13 trillion dollars, and daily trading volumes were up 44 percent year over year. Margin loan balances jumped 93 percent year over year to nearly 188 billion dollars as of quarter end — that is a significant engagement signal.

PNC beat on earnings per share at five-09 adjusted versus four-96, helped by provisions coming in at 189 million versus the 246 million estimate. But revenue missed slightly and the 2026 expense guidance moved higher to 9.5 percent growth from 8.5 percent — so the quality of the beat is a bit mixed. US Bancorp was essentially inline, with the full-year guide nudged higher on revenue and operating leverage — constructive but not exciting.

Marsh beat by a few cents with strong consulting organic growth of 8 percent against a 4.8 percent estimate, though Reinsurance was soft. First Horizon reported a headline loss but the underlying adjusted number was inline — the balance sheet restructuring, selling roughly four-and-a-half billion of lower-yielding mortgages, should be accretive going forward.

Now the bad news. FMC Corporation issued a major negative preannouncement. The company is aggressively cutting prices on products sitting in channel inventory and overhauling its US pricing model entirely. Management cited weaker-than-expected demand and elevated inventory at channel customers blocking replenishment. This is the kind of preannouncement that can reprice an entire subsector — watch agricultural chemicals broadly.

On the consumer side, Kimberly-Clark was mixed — earnings per share beat at one-70 versus one-60, but organic sales fell 1.3 percent against an estimate of negative 0.7 percent, with full-year guidance simply reiterated. Not a catalyst to get excited about. Penske Auto is going private at 212 dollars per share in a 16.3 billion dollar deal with Penske Corp and Mitsui — straightforward buyout premium.

Manpower was inline and the Q4 guide came in just slightly below the Street. Management is calling 2026 an inflection year but the numbers don't fully confirm that yet.

Bottom line for today: financials are the story, and the tone there is generally positive. But watch FMC and the ag-chem space for spillover weakness. No macro catalyst on the calendar in this note, so earnings reactions will drive price action.
